proof.text: Lift the recorded ring-sheaf coefficient isomorphism to commutative ring sheaves by keeping its sectionwise ring homomorphisms. Faithfulness proves its inverse laws. The restriction along this explicit lift is definitionally the recorded fdCoefficientTransport.

Apply ringIso_tensor_transport to the explicit lift. Its braided structure supplies the invertible ordinary tensor map, its pure_hom field is exactly the required local pure-tensor formula, and oplax monoidal naturality supplies simultaneous naturality.

For uniqueness, precompose a competing comparison by the inverse of the constructed comparison. Its action on every target pure tensor is the identity, by the two pure-tensor formulas and the inverse law. The sheafification adjunction reduces equality of maps out of a sheaf tensor to equality on presheaf pure tensors; the module tensor extensionality theorem finishes. Function and isomorphism extensionality give equality of the families.

Read naturality from the unique witness used to define moduleComparison. The tensorHom formula is definitionally the same naturality identity. The definition total is the unchanged inverse-comparison direct-sum construction tensorPullbackTotal, with the source, target, and additive instances explicitly fixed.

The equivalence in ringIso_tensor_transport makes the recorded coefficient restriction a left adjoint. Apply tensorPullbackTotal_isIso with its adjunction to the selected moduleComparison and its proved tensorHom naturality. The theorem proves invertibility of this actual signed-total map, since left adjoints preserve its coproducts. Inverting asIso gives totalIso in the required orientation.

title: Pure-tensor coefficient comparison and its signed total
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension, and $X$ a scheme. Use the quotient-normalized completed coefficient ring isomorphism and its exact scalar-restriction functor $A$ [def-fd-coefficient-comparison-datum]. The ordinary coefficient tensor comparison is the unique natural family $A(M\otimes N)\simeq A(M)\otimes A(N)$ for module sheaves [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] sending every local pure tensor $x\otimes y$ to the same tensor of the restricted sections. On cochain complexes, define its inverse signed-total comparison by the universal direct-sum map: its restriction to the $(p,q)$-summand is the inverse ordinary module tensor comparison followed by $A$ applied to the $(p,q)$-summand inclusion. Exact scalar restriction preserves these direct sums, so this chain map is invertible; the forward total comparison is its inverse. The differential uses the recorded sign $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_Q$ [def-weil-derived-tensor]. No completion is applied in this comparison.
